title: 23.3 EdgeDiff: 418.4mJ/Inference Multi-Modal Few-Step Diffusion Model Accelerator with Mixed-Precision and Reordered Group Quantization
problem: Few-step diffusion models (FSDM) for mobile image generation lack redundancy between denoising steps (unlike standard DMs), and introduce computational bottlenecks in multi-modal encoders/decoders that are sensitive to quantization precision.
motivation: Mobile devices demand on-device image generation, but standard diffusion model accelerators cannot exploit inter-timestep redundancy in FSDMs, and multi-modal FSDMs introduce encoder/decoder bottlenecks requiring careful precision management.
method: EdgeDiff compresses few-step diffusion models using two quantization techniques applied across the encoder, UNet, and decoder: mixed-precision quantization, which stores different model parts with different numbers of bits (giving more bits to sensitive components like the encoder and decoder), and reordered group quantization, which groups similar weights and finds the best grouping order for efficient compression. Unlike standard diffusion models, few-step models lack redundancy between denoising steps, so this approach focuses on optimizing each component's compression tolerance directly rather than exploiting temporal patterns. The result is efficient mobile inference while preserving accuracy in the sensitive multi-modal components.
key_novelty: EdgeDiff accelerates few-step diffusion inference by combining mixed-precision quantization (using different bit-widths for different model parts) with reordered group quantization (optimizing weight groupings), without relying on inter-timestep redundancy.
contributions: Reordered group quantization reducing precision loss
Efficient encoder/decoder processing for multi-modal models
limitations: Abstract-only; image quality metrics (FID, LPIPS), latency breakdown, memory bandwidth requirements, and accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs not discussed.
primary_theme: Mixed-precision few-step diffusion accelerator for edge image generation
